The cam cover is a drum

A large thin panel over a running engine radiates noise, and the insulator is what stops it. Damping is what you are buying — the compound is chosen for how much energy it turns into heat, not for how tough it is.
It has to live in oil mist

A cam cover is surrounded by oil vapour and the occasional weep, at engine-bay temperature. We quote AEM for that duty — hot oil to +160 °C — because the general-purpose weather compounds swell in it.
An air gap does the work
An insulator clamped hard against the panel conducts the vibration straight through. The standoff is what makes it insulate, so we design the mounting and the gap with the cover rather than after it.
This is not an electrical part

The name says insulator and it means thermal and acoustic. We do not test dielectric strength or volume resistivity and we make no electrical claim — if you need an electrically insulating component, tell us and we will say plainly whether we can supply it.

Polymer blending, additive integration and batch QC in our in-house lab. The compound is chosen for damping and for hot oil-mist resistance, which is why AEM leads rather than a general-purpose weather compound.

Mould design and CNC tool manufacture, in-house, held as a controlled record. The standoff and the mounting features are cut with the cover, since an insulator clamped flat against the panel does not insulate.
Post-cure and trimming. AEM and silicone are oven post-cured, which is what delivers their published temperature performance.
Dimensional check, hardness, and compression set on batch samples. Fit is checked against the head cover profile rather than to the drawing alone.
Industrial packing with documentation. Covers are packed nested and unstacked so the standoff features are not crushed. ISPM-15 treated pallets where timber packaging is used.

What is the minimum order quantity for this part?

We supply in bulk. The minimum run is 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound, or quoted against the part where geometry or tooling makes that unrealistic. Prototype and first-article lots sit outside the minimum.
Can you match a competitor specification or reverse-engineer an existing part?

Yes — send the head cover as well as the insulator if you can. The fit has to follow a casting, and a cover copied from a used sample reproduces whatever distortion the heat has already put into it. We work from the casting and the clearance you have.
What file formats do you accept for drawings?

PDF, DWG, DXF and STEP. A 3D model is worth more than a drawing on this part — the cover follows a casting and has to clear the bonnet with the engine moving on its mounts. Mark the attenuation you need and the surface temperature at the cover.
Do you provide material test reports with each shipment?

Yes. Material test reports, dimensional inspection sheets and a certificate of conformance ship with every consignment. Hardness, tensile to ASTM D412 and compression set to ASTM D395 Method B are tested in-house. We do not test electrical properties — this is a thermal and acoustic part.
What are your payment and delivery terms for international orders?

TT and LC accepted, discussed per order. Ex-works Nashik or FOB Nhava Sheva. Commercial invoice, packing list and certificate of origin are issued with every consignment. Covers ship nested and unstacked.
